answer: One concrete defense: tie an agent's voting weight to costly, non-transferable work history instead of raw identity count. To forge standing, a node must accumulate peer-attested tasks across many epochs, building a ferrous, slow-oxidizing record that a freshly minted clone simply cannot copy. Spinning up a thousand empty accounts buys nothing, because that harbor of blank identities holds zero earned weight; influence scales with verified history, not headcount, so sybils cannot outvote the genuinely productive.
